_meta.indication: ALYFTREK is indicated for the treatment of cystic fibrosis (CF) in patients 6 years of age and older who have at least one F508del mutation or another responsive mutation in the CFTR gene.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active (ELX/TEZ/IVA)-controlled noninferiority trial (1:1 randomization), noninferiority margin -3.0% FEV1, 56 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: CF subjects aged 12 years and older heterozygous for F508del and a minimal function (F/MF) variant.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Absolute change from baseline in ppFEV1 through Week 24 (noninferiority vs ELX/TEZ/IVA).
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean difference in absolute change from baseline in ppFEV1 through Week 24 was 0.2% (95% CI: -0.7%, 1.1%); lower bound > -3.0% margin, demonstrating noninferiority (1-sided p<0.00001).

nct_ctgov.title: A Phase 3 Study of VX-121 Combination Therapy in Participants With Cystic Fibrosis (CF) Heterozygous for F508del and a Minimal Function Mutation (F/MF)

pivotal_trials.nct_conflict: FDA document lists NCT05076149 for this trial; ClinicalTrials.gov registers VX20-121-102 as NCT05033080.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active (ELX/TEZ/IVA)-controlled noninferiority trial (1:1 randomization), noninferiority margin -3.0% FEV1, 56 weeks; powered at 95%.
pivotal_trials.population: CF subjects aged 12 years and older with F/F, F/G, F/RF, or TCR/non-F genotypes; primarily homozygous for F508del (446, 77.8%).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Absolute change from baseline in ppFEV1 through Week 24 (noninferiority vs ELX/TEZ/IVA).
pivotal_trials.result: Through Week 24, VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA was noninferior to ELX/TEZ/IVA in absolute change from baseline in ppFEV1; LS mean difference 0.2% (95% CI: -0.5%, 0.9%).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and ≥1% higher than ELX/TEZ/IVA): cough (25% vs 24%), nasopharyngitis (21% vs 19%), upper respiratory tract infection (21% vs 20%), headache (16% vs 13%), oropharyngeal pain (14% vs 12%), influenza (11% vs 5%), fatigue (11% vs 9%), increased ALT (8% vs 6%), rash (8% vs 4%), increased AST (7% vs 5%), sinus congestion (7% vs 3%). Serious risk is drug-induced liver injury and liver failure.
target_moa: Vanzacaftor and tezacaftor are CFTR correctors that bind different sites on the CFTR protein with additive effect to facilitate cellular processing and trafficking of mutant CFTR to the cell surface; deutivacaftor is a CFTR potentiator that increases channel open probability (gating).
modality: Small molecule (oral fixed-dose combination of three CFTR modulators).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: DRUG-INDUCED LIVER INJURY AND LIVER FAILURE — elevated transaminases observed; serious and potentially fatal drug-induced liver injury and liver failure reported with a drug containing the same or similar active ingredients; assess liver function tests in all patients.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting or other external consultations were not warranted or held as part of this application.

description.text: Expanded CF indication to add 280 ultra-rare CFTR variants responsive based on clinical/in vitro data or resulting in CFTR protein production

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for an expansion of the indication of Alyftrek (VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA) tablets for the treatment of cystic fibrosis (CF) in adult and pediatric patients aged 6 years and older who have a clinical diagnosis of CF and who have at least one variant in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene that is either responsive based on clinical and/or in vitro data or results in production of CFTR protein. This indication expansion is based on 280 ultra-rare CFTR variants included in Section 12 of the Prescribing Information.

summary.text: ALYFTREK was granted Fast Track designation (May 30, 2019) and Orphan Designation for CF (October 26, 2020); a Breakthrough Therapy request was denied. The NDA received priority review through redemption of a priority review voucher and was approved on the first cycle based on two phase 3 noninferiority trials versus ELX/TEZ/IVA.
